clue.text: Degree of confidence the writer includes in speech

indicators.note: includes means the first piece wraps around the second one here

parts.note: the writer is the setter referring to themselves, giving ME
something done in speech is oral, spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A speaker's level of self-assurance shows when an author slips something into a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the level of confidence and spirit in a person or group.

clue.text: Completely holding game up with hubris

indicators.note: holding says the first word keeps the second inside it

parts.note: arrant means utter or complete, so arrantly means completely

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a game entirely out of overweening pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely' looks like an adverb on 'holding', but it is the fodder; 'up' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with hubris means acting with excessive pride, which is behaving haughtily and conceitedly.

clue.text: After switching ends, may dread such distracting thoughts

indicators.note: switching ends says the phrase's opening and closing letters trade places, a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone fears their idle reveries, but the clue twists the words themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearrangement is a precise one: only the M at the front and the D at the back of the phrase change places.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydreams are idle reveries that distract the mind from the task in hand.

clue.text: King in opposite of 3 in June?

definitions.text: King in opposite of 3 in June?

parts.words: King in opposite of 3 in June?
parts.note: the opposite of a daydream is a night's dream, and one set in June is A Midsummer Night's Dream, whose fairy king is wanted

explanation.surface: A monarch appears in whatever is the reverse of a June reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is DAYDREAM; swapping day for night and adding midsummer (June) points to Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: In the event, shoe covers nothing after top comes off

indicators.note: covers says the shoe word goes around the other piece
the top of a down entry is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a moccasin is a soft leather shoe
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: In some situation a shoe gets covered, once its upper part has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after top comes off' drops M from MOCCASIN to leave OCCASIN, and O goes in before its final N. 'In the' merely leads in.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular event or happening.

clue.text: Resort by the sea — they help sightseers relax

definitions.text: Resort by the sea — they help sightseers relax

parts.words: Resort by the sea — they help sightseers relax
parts.note: read as baths beside the 'see' organ: little cups used to rinse and soothe the organs of sight

explanation.surface: A seaside spa town is a place where tourists unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a spa resort, and the clue's sightseers are simply people who see, whose eyes are refreshed by these cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebaths are small cups for bathing the eyes, soothing tired organs of sight.

clue.text: What leads to destruction in theatrical location?

definitions.meaning: in the Sermon on the Mount, broad is the way that leads to destruction (Matthew 7:13)
the New York street famous for its theatres

explanation.surface: Asks what leads to ruin in the world of show business.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway in New York is the heart of American theatre, and the biblical broad way leads to destruction.

clue.text: As is everything that ends thus, dramatically

definitions.text: As is everything that ends thus, dramatically

parts.words: As is everything that ends thus, dramatically
parts.note: points to a Shakespeare comedy title, All's ___ That Ends ___, where the missing word appears twice

explanation.surface: A remark that all is fine if it finishes in a theatrical way.
explanation.definitionFit: The play title says all's well that ends well, so everything ending that way is satisfactory.

clue.text: Period that's long, but finally cut

indicators.note: finally cut says the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it

explanation.surface: A stretch of time that seems lengthy is eventually brought to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the period, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of twelve months.

clue.text: "Brute" finished his final speech

parts.note: the dying words 'Et tu, Brute?' end the last speech of the Roman leader stabbed by Brutus

explanation.surface: A savage person completed a farewell address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brute' looks like a thug, but it is the Latin vocative of Brutus in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's last words in the play are 'Et tu, Brute? Then fall, Caesar!'

clue.text: Lamb put on string for princess

indicators.note: in an across clue, put on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: string is cord
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A young sheep is tethered to a line on behalf of a royal daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' wants to be the animal; it is Charles Lamb, who wrote as Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordelia is King Lear's youngest daughter, a princess in the play.

clue.text: Bard pronounced tribal leader's equal

indicators.note: pronounced says the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab tribal leader, and his equal is his peer: sheikh's peer

explanation.surface: A poet is declared to be on a par with a chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard is the customary title for Shakespeare, England's greatest poet.

clue.text: Increases number of articles on stage, including gemstone

indicators.note: including says the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: props are the objects used by actors on stage
agate is a banded semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: A theatre adds more objects to the set, a jewel among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate living things is to breed them, multiplying their number.

clue.text: Unusually precise about line for title role

indicators.note: about says the rearranged word goes round the other letter
unusually says the letters are set out in an odd order

explanation.surface: An oddly exact remark concerning a line for the lead part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' signals the rearrangement of 'precise' before the line letter goes in; 'title role' works because the play is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles, Prince of Tyre is a Shakespeare play named after its hero.

clue.text: Weapon as woman's precarious sole means of support?

definitions.meaning: a short dagger with a narrow blade

definitions.text: woman's precarious sole means of support?
definitions.meaning: a tall thin heel on a woman's shoe, all that holds up the sole

explanation.surface: A woman with only a weapon is precariously supporting herself.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is both a slender dagger and a high, thin shoe heel named after it.

clue.text: Turned to unbearable torment? Love is, for him

indicators.note: turned says the little word is read backwards

parts.note: hell is unbearable torment
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Love drives a man to agony beyond bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The play's hero is driven by jealous love to torment, so 'him' points to the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Moor whose love turns to torment; the clue's pronoun refers to him.

clue.text: Non-U sound of bovine pupils

parts.note: to low is to make the deep sound of a cow
a group of pupils taught together is a class

explanation.surface: Cows' students make a vulgar noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is British slang for socially lower-class usage; U meant upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U describes manners or speech not of the upper class, so of humbler status.

clue.text: Dramatic storm

parts.note: a violent gale that is also the title of a play, Shakespeare's last solo work

explanation.surface: A theatrically violent gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and The Tempest is a Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Wife and a youth confused by 11's alternative title

indicators.note: confused means the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: 11 is SHAKESPEARE, whose first name is Will

explanation.surface: A spouse and a young man are muddled by the playwright's second name for a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelfth Night's subtitle, Or What You Will, is an alternative title for that play.

clue.text: United Nations upholding a role for American statesman

annotationWithheld.why: United Nations upholding a role for American statesman (6): UN around A HAT read upwards needs 'upholding' both as the container and as the reversal indicator, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: United Nations upholding a role for American statesman

clue.text: A bird others upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: the other birds here are auks, seabirds of the same coasts

explanation.surface: A bird annoys its neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory seabird that robs other birds of food.

clue.text: Joiner with arms raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: arms are weapons, such as guns

explanation.surface: A carpenter holds up his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' wants to be limbs; it is weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug the joiner is the craftsman who plays the Lion in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Character with family, tragically regal

parts.note: one's kin are one's family

indicators.note: tragically says the word's letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A person and their relatives are royal in a tragic way.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Bad actor allowed title role

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A poor performer is given the lead part.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, title character of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Antonio's vessels from ancient city that is to south

parts.note: Argos is an ancient city in Greece

explanation.surface: A merchant's ships come from an old Greek city lying to the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Argosies are large merchant ships; Antonio's argosies are lost in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Officer protects fool, one in role of lieutenant

indicators.note: protects says the first piece shelters the others inside it

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A commander shields an idiot, one serving as his deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant, whom Iago schemes against.
